content: LLM-generated tests have measurably weak fault detection: mutation-testing scores for LLM-generated tests peak around 0.546 vs 0.690 for human-written tests, meaning tests pass but do not actually kill mutants/catch bugs. Same-model bias is empirically documented: LLM solutions perform substantially better on their own self-generated tests than on independent test suites (e.g. AtCoder study), meaning a model's blind spots in the solution are mirrored as blind spots in its tests. Bulk-generated test sets also have low retention/validity rate against ground truth (often under 60% usable), so naive 'generate N tests' without independent verification produces false confidence.
